Yato... she can be scary, but we have a purr-omise! She won't just leave me like this.
N-No need to worry! I'll just wait here for them to find meow.
Mrow! Help!
I-In the forest...
Biologist of the Scriveners, future authority on Terra... are all nine of my lives going to end here?
No! I-I'll—
I... I won't go off on meow own again...
I won't call Noir Corne stupid anymore... I'll purr-aise Smithy from time to time... I mean, all the time!
Somebody... anybody... help... meow...
What are you doing, Scholar?
Mrow?
I... Meow did you...
You idiot! Stupid Noir Corne! Hornhead!
Huh? What did I do?
You're interrupting the ecological research of the meow-vellous scholar furmerly of the Royal Pawleontology Scriveners!
Er... could you repeat that?
There's a time and a place, people. We've been trapped here for more than two hours.
The sun's about to set. We should be spending our time looking for a way out, not arguing.
...Talk, Scholar! What were you researching?
None of your business!
Let me see... Yato! There are carvings on the bark!
'Record of abnormality in the hills...'
'Visual references unreliable. Follow the wind. -Mirai'
Must be someone who came before us. The message is telling us to follow the wind.
Mrow? It was writing then?
You found this? Not bad, Scholar! Looks like I underestimated you!
I... Mrow! What do mew mean you underestimated me?
The wind...
We can see which way the wind is blowing by sprinkling that dust from up high.
Good idea. Let's try it.
Let me take another look at the carving. Doesn't look like it's been too long... What's this 'Mirai'?
Hey! Wait for me!
We're finally out of it.
It's a lake. No wonder the wind was purring.
Hold it. Looks like there's a camp by the shore. There might be someone there.
Stay here while I check it out...
Camp! Campfire! Barbecue! Let's get those paws moving!
Meow!
Finally got the fire lit.
This camp hasn't been used for ages. Must have been left behind by hunters. Good thing the stuff here still works.
...Alright, I guess it's harder to move at night, or spot the Rathalos's tracks.
We can rest here for a little bit, but after that we need to keep moving.
Alright, alright.
Hehe...
What are you laughing about?
Nothing... Well, just that you never change. You're always in a rush, like you're being chased by somebody.
We've been following the Doctor's orders for so long now, yet not a bit of their calmness has rubbed off on you.
They would want us to achieve our mission as soon as possible.
Fine, fine. You win.
Why don't you listen to me the way you used to, close your eyes, get some rest, and we'll set out again in the morning, fully refreshed?
I'll search the camp for anything useful.
Rest...?
Looks like the headman wasn't lying. There are no hunters left around here, other than old Kashiwau.
This must have something to do with that big cave that we went into. Maybe with old Kashiwau's temper too...
We'll know when we find the Rathalos. If you've got the time to worry about all this nonsense, then we might as well set out now.
Fine... Yuck, the box is covered in dust. The lock's all rusted through too. Let me see...
Hey, lots of hunting equipment... machetes, knives, traps, and some solid ropes.
Take everything that looks useful.
A spear, too. Looks like the same kind that old Kashiwau carries with him.
I've seen ones like that around here. The locals use them for hunting.
This one's broken, though. No spearhead in the box either. What do you think?
Hm...
What is it?
I'm surprised at how elaborate it is.
The core of the handle has been hollowed out. Is that a bowstring in it? It's made from animal hair, pretty solid.
I see... the switch on the handle controls the bowstring, allowing the spear to be thrown with great force, judging by the length of the string.
The broken part is a swivel. Seems like the spear can be turned in a certain direction, or locked, allowing the wielder to deal with different combat situations.
...The designer knew what they were doing.
Well, you're the expert when it comes to weapons.
Here, put it back. It's no use to us.
Hey, wait, there are words engraved in the handle.
Akira Kashiwau... is that the owner of the spear?
Old Kashiwau's given name is Yoshitaka. A relative of his? I'll see if there's anything else.
Corne... Huh? What's that on the ground?
What? Let me see.
A photo. It must have fallen out of the box when you opened it.
A gathering of hunters... there's a date on the lower corner. It's from nine years ago.
Is that the headman on the right? Did he use to be a hunter too?
I suppose so.
He looks completely different in hunter garb. There's a little girl standing to his right.
Hey, look at the guy over here!
Don't shout like that.
He's the only one in the photo carrying a spear. Looks like the one that's broken, too.
Akira Kashiwau... could it be him? He looks pretty young. Wouldn't quite be middle-aged, even after nine years.
But I don't remember anyone like him in the village. How about you, Yato?
Nope.
So it's a gathering of hunters, but old Kashiwau isn't in it?
Maybe he just wasn't there for the photo. Put it back.
Headman Takii looks so young!
Did he not get along with the others, even back then? But the younger Kashiwau in this photo looks pretty close to him.
There was a hunter statue in the village, but it hasn't been tended to for a long time. And the headman used to be a hunter... Could this all be because of Akira Kashiwau?
Corne!
Oh...
That's enough.
What does this photo have to do with our mission? Does it matter who's in it or not, or how many people or burdenbeasts there are in the Kashiwau household?
It means nothing to us.
Our missions take longer than they should because you always get distracted by these things.
Even if we could figure out what happened to the old man's family, what does it change?
Are you going to give him counselling? What about the others? Are you going to win them over with love and understanding?
You saw the people in the village... and that child...
The people here are unknowingly walking towards the abyss. The best we can do is save their lives, no more and no less.
And the faster we find the Rathalos, the closer we get to the truth, and the better our odds of stopping Oripathy from spreading in the village.
We must work harder... do everything we can to ensure their safety. That's our mission, our duty.
And you need to understand that, Corne— No, Operator Noir Corne.
I know, I know. Don't get so angry.
It's just that I can't help but think about old Kashiwau.
The things he said, the things he did... that inexplicable stubbornness, his insistence on facing everything on his own... It's as if he's running away from something.
Have you forgotten? It's just like...
No, never mind.
Anyway, I can't prove it yet, but I wouldn't be so sure that none of this has anything to do with our mission.
Very well, Operator Noir Corne, in that case I'm giving you an order, as captain of Operations Team A4.
You will refrain from concerning yourself with matters unrelated to the mission objective, until such time that there is evidence suggesting otherwise.
...Yes, ma'am.
Good.
...Yato.
I'm... I'm worried about you too.
I'll check the surrounding area for threats. We'll leave once we're rested.
Noir Corne is making me catch fish while he goes and purr-lays with the campfire!
They're called Fins.
Based on their appearance and my im-purr-essive knowledge, they're the same exact thing!
♪Throw a buoy, let it float, meow♪
♪Knock knock, meow♪
Remember what I said this afternoon, Smithy?
I looked through my notes on the ecology of Terra and I realize why something didn't seem right, mrow.
There are no meownsters in this forest!
Where we came from, there are always meownsters in the wild. What do the scholars say again...?
Yes, balance. They balance the environment, mrow.
But we haven't seen any creatures like that here. It's so strange.
And those rampaging hornbeasts. They stripped the bark clean off the trees wherever their paws took them. Do you realize what that means?
Mrow?
Silly Smithy. It means things were not always like this, otherwise the trees couldn't have grown.
The ecological order of the forest was destabilized at some point.
Something... went meowssing.
But not to worry! With you and I here, they can deal with the Rathalos, even if they're not so strong!
Hey, are you listening, Smithy?
♪Knock knock, meow♪
I shouldn't have had you do this!
♪Knock knock, meow♪
The fincatching buoy isn't moving at all! Are there really any fish in this pond?
Did you catch any Fins, Scholar?
Purrfect timing! Sit here.
Take this.
The fincatching rod? Why?
Don't meowve.
Stay!
...What are you doing?
Watching you fish.
Why, you—oh!
The buoy sank!
It's so heavy! What do I do?
Pull! Pull hard!
They're dead... because of you...
Stop running... Yato...
Because of you...
Argh! W-Why...? It happened so long ago...
Noir Corne!
Four turns! No more than that!
Look, I was watching this whole time, and it hasn't changed color at all... whoa!
Okay, now it has!
And now it's burnt...
Your own fault for not listening! You eat it!
My fault? It's all because you distracted me...
Mroaaaw!
Hey! Stop scratching my horn!
*Sigh*...
Mrrow...
Shouldn't you be saving your strength for the Rathalos? Don't let me catch you running away as soon as we get a glimpse.
I told you, I know purrcisely how to deal with the Rathalos. I've noted its weaknesses in my notebook.
It's just that your weapons are too weak. Good thing I had the purresence of mind to tell Smithy to meowke stronger weapons.
Rathalos... I wonder what its meat tastes like...
I tell you, Rathalos liver is pawsitively delicious! Nothing is tastier!
*Huff*...
—! Who goes there?!
Yato? Where are you going?
I saw a shadow in the corner of my eye. It went this way.
Who's there? Come out!
I know you're there.
(Where did they go?)
Meow...
(Over there!)
I'll give you one chance to show yourself.
(Approaches slowly)
You...
Show yourself right now!
Meow! It's Yato!
Artisan? It was you?
Mrow?
No, it couldn't be... the one I saw was...
Are they gone?
Yato—
Y-You're too fast...
Did you see something?
Yes, but I lost them.
What are you doing here, Arty?
Knocking on meowterials.
You're making... armor and weapons? For the fight against the Rathalos?
Don't touch it!
No stone! Use this instead!
Is that really something that can be swapped just like that?
Click! There.
Equipment for two!
You want us to put them on?
Purrt them on! Better against Rathalos!
It's worth a shot.
Well, I for one can't wait!
...You change over there, Corne.
How do I... put this on?
Does my arm go through here?
And why is it so...?
I've never... worn anything like this before.
Am I wearing this right? I can't tell.
The helmet's so heavy... and stuffy... is this right?
Ouch! And why are there spikes here? They're even longer than my horn.
Is this really meant for wearing?
(The material is light, but surprisingly tough.)
(Arty said they made it using Rathalos parts they brought with them. Not even Yato could cut through it...)
(But something feels familiar about this material.)
(Where have I seen it before? I just can't remember.)
Yato? I'm done over here. Where are you?
I'm coming! Whoa—
Ow, I hit my head... And now I can't see anything.
Did it go like this? Finally got it on right.
(Looks at Yato)
Oh...
Light, swift, powerful.
That's what I always tell people when I talk about this strange new gear afterwards.
'That's not what we were asking about!'
And that's the answer I always get from other operators.
I still don't understand what they mean.
Its showing so much skin... Is this really supposed to be protective gear?
But... I do feel a strange tingling on my skin. And my discomfort from the light is gone.
Look at that, Kirin set!
Kirin set? Is that what this is called?
Mrow.
...I suppose I should ask Leizi about it.
Terra meowterial's not bad! Good substitute.
(Whisper) ...Thanks, Originium slugs.
My new blades need to be tested in battle... Corne?
What are you doing on the ground?
I... I tripped. Not used to this new gear.
Wait, your mask...
I took it off. Doesn't seem like I'll need it to block out the light with this gear, and it's extra weight I don't need.
What... What are you staring at?
Nothing!
...Get up. We can't afford to be caught off guard out here. Get used to it quickly.
O-Okay!
Yato! Noir Corne!
That strange old man came!
He took your gear!
Your hatred for dried blood will cause your spearhead to rust and go dull.
Tonight will be the same as that night. There will be but a single moon in the lake.
The reflection of the moonlight, weak and powerless, always hiding in the back... If only things had gone in a different direction...
Ah... It's too quiet.
The calmest nights are always the cruelest, for that is when those who should not have been forgotten are dragged to the surface of our memories.
You must remember... I told you this before. We often rested at the campsite by the lake, sat around the campfire, and discussed how to deal with the beasts.
The crackling, the turning barbecue, the melting fat. I remember.
I... I will never forget any of it.
It's time. Let's not keep the beast waiting any longer.
Hm? A fire from that direction...
The abandoned camp?!
Who could be there?
Someone cooked here...
This fire...
The Terran night sky looks just about the same as ours... but the stars apurr to be in completely different pawsitions.
Mrow... So meowny strange clouds covering the sky tonight, like nothing I've ever seen. I should note this down.
From what Noir Corne has told me, Terra's climate is not meowch different from ours.
Wind, thunderstorms, rain, and snow... Similar environments have similar natural cycles. Nothing strange about that.
But he also mentioned a phenomeownon called... Catastrophes? What could be so cat-astrophic to deserve a name like that?
If his description is accurate, then they're as terrifying and destructive as the Amatsu turning out, only caused by this Originium they seem so obsessed with...
How could rocks pawssibly be the cause of anything when they can't even move? I can't make heads or tails of how this works.
Not that I'm one to acknowledge a phenomeownon I've never observed myself, but... it seems nearly everything unique about Terra has to do with Originium.
Oh... If only I could see a Catastrophe with meow own eyes...
Mrow? Is Noir Corne back?
Huh? Who's that...?

lines.st: The fire illuminates the elderly man's face.
The ravines, though eroded away by the past...
seem far more ancient than everything he's been through.
He cannot remember how long ago it was.
The campfire before him feels just as hot as it did then.
Time once burnt away rouses once again those muddled voices.
He cannot tell if it is he or the earth which is shaking...

lines.x: Akira...
Akira.
Hah, you're not dead yet, old timer.
Indeed, not yet.
Unlike you, these fierce but dull-witted beasts will never defeat me.
Life is stubborn, huh? That's what you think? Just like those beasts who keep crawling forward even with their skulls pierced?
Not bad. You think that's what you've become.
Listen up. I will keep hunting.
It doesn't matter if there are a hundred, a thousand, or even ten thousand of those beasts in the forest. I won't stop until they're all dead.
It doesn't matter what I am up against... One by one, I will kill each and every one of them with my own two hands.
I have to hunt the big one now. I have no time to deal with you or your word games.
*cough*—Scratch marks, and huge ones, too.
It must've been here not too long ago... It's hungry, and it's on the hunt.
You don't stand a chance tonight.
Preposterous.
You're old and battered, and you've just been through a brutal struggle. Plus, it's raining, and there's no one to help you here.
If you keep going like this, you will die. You're no wild beast. You know that.
I'm not like you... I won't go down so easily.
You know who you are.
...Look at these fallen leaves. If I cover these marks with them, no one will know they weren't washed here by the rain.
No one else will find its tracks. This hunt is mine and mine alone.
Really, old timer, sometimes I don't get what the point of all this is.
So now you're going to criticize me?
All I did was take your place and do what you would.
Really now?
Chasing beasts into the forest like it's the end of the world... hacking and slashing at them, carving out their hearts, and coming home covered in cuts and bruises...
You used to blabber about hunting day in and day out. Isn't that what you loved the most?
Even after all this time, you still don't understand me.
Oh? I don't understand you? Then what about you? Do you think you all your actions were correct?
You've never once listened to what I say. Have you ever tried to understand how I feel? Even once?
That night, if you had listened to even a single word I said...
If you hadn't charged into this damnable forest, you wouldn't have turned into an unrecognizable pile of minced meat.
And I would never have left you behind like those guys did.
Do you still not understand? Everything that I do... I'm doing it for you.
No, Yoshitaka, you're doing it for yourself.
And you know it.
He can't hear your voice.
We meet again, Kashiwau.
So that was you...
I warned you not to enter the forest.
We're free to come and go as we please. We have no reason to be intimidated by you.
You stubborn kids don't know what's good for you... You don't know what real fear is!
You will die! Do you get it? Die!
Maybe. But more importantly, nothing can scare us off from completing our mission.
And may I ask you to set down what you're holding?
This is my hunting equipment... Mine, you thieves!
Feel free to take what's yours, but please put down the things that belong to us.
You won't need them, and that's because you're leaving this forest right this instant! Don't even think about getting in my way!
Preposterous.
Alright, I see now... You're just here to make trouble for me, aren't you? You want to take everything from me, don't you? Just like them.
You're overthinking this. I'm only worried about your safety.
You see, Kashiwau, you came here too. Which means we share the same objective.
I don't understand why you feel the way you do, and naturally I don't need to know either.
But I have a suggestion. Let's set aside our differences and work together. We can solve a lot of problems that way.
Not a chance! That quarry is mine and nobody else's!
In that case, I ask only that you not interfere with our work anymore.
Furthermore, considering we have the same objective, your actions will likely affect us one way or another...
So I suggest you wait at the camp until daybreak. You're free to return to the village after that.
Yato, that's a bit...
You... How dare you!
Begone! Crawl back to wherever you came from!
I refuse.
Hold on, you two.
I... I'll have the lot of you...
I see it!
Smithy, what do you see?
Hunters! You need to leave this place and put out that campfire immediately!
That voice... You're...!
The firelight has attracted the Rathalos's attention. It'll come attacking any second now!
The Rathalos?
Rathalos!
What?
Yato, are you alright?
It's strange... These blades... They should be effective against the Rathalos, but I'm not getting anywhere with them.
Why? Am I not using them correctly?
Corne, cover me! I'll try again!
Got it! Ah, hold up! I don't have my shield! And what do I do with this blade—
Wait—You! Argh, whatever! I'm coming!
Scholar, do you have a plan yet?
Patience! I'm thinking! Don't rush meow!
The Rathalos's weakness... the Rathalos's attack patterns... That's not it... I remeowmber copying something about this from the Hunter's Notes. Where did I purrt them?
Are you sure you can handle this?
Corne, the Rathalos is coming your way! Watch out!
I'll just raise my—Where's my shield?
Dodge left, your meowjesty!
Long Swords require excellent control. You need to channel your inner energy to use them effectively. Victory is determined at the moment you unleash your attack.
That voice... It's the same one I heard earlier... Argh!
Er, what is this?
Stupid Noir Corne! That's a Felyne too. A Palico!
Horned foreign Hunter. I'm a Palico with years of experience... Mrow.
Yato, it's going to breathe fire again!
But look at that head, Scholar! Is that really a Felyne?
This armor was gifted to me by a Hunter whom I followed faithfully for years. It is the very embodiment of our countless hunts together, a symbol of bravery and experience... Mrow.
Yeah, I'm not getting any of that from it! And Scholar, why is there a Felyne fighting? I know you've been running away every time there's a fight!
You fool, that's a Palico! They're in charge of all the hunting!
Palicoes accompany Hunters on their hunts as partners. It is an age-old tradition. And not one limited to just Felynes. Supposedly, certain eastern villages train their Canynes to join in on their—
What are all of you doing?! Corne! Get it together!
I got it! Okay, lemme think. Control... Control...
Haaahhh! I got this! Take that!
It really worked!
Now's our chance!
Kashiwau! What are you doing? Why did you push me away?
This beast is mine to slay!
Out of my way! All of you!
Yato, it's coming again!
Monster! Look over here!
Noir Corne, I have an idea!
It's written in my notes that when using meowlee weapons, a Rathalos's head is its greatest weakness, followed by its wings and its tail!
The most important attack to watch for is its tailspin! It will sweep its tail to attack after confirming the position. So when you see it tilt its head, that's the direction it'll swing its tail!
So we take advantage of the time it takes for its enormous body to readjust? Got it. Just like how Corne and I tried it the last time.
I cannot say for sure if it will work. There's been something abnormal about this Rathalos ever since it made its way here...
Regardless, it's worth a try. I'll strike.
I'll try to bait its tailspin then. Palico, you're more nimble than me. When it starts attacking, can you run interference?
I shall try my best... Mrow.
Ah! Old man Kashiwau's rushing in again. Scholar, stop him!
And meow am I supposed to do that?
Whatever, here goes! Hyah!
That's the sign that it's about to tailspin!
(An opening...)
(Now!)
Wait, this doesn't feel right... Mrow!
The Rathalos noticed Yato's attack... How is that pawssible?
It didn't even look...
Is that... Originium dust surrounding it?!
Watch out, Yato! It's about to breathe fire!
Phew... If I'd taken that head on, I'd probably be...
I've never heard of a Rathalos that could breathe terrifying flames like that!
I'm pawsitive there's nothing like that in my records...
Yato! It's charging your way again!
No, wait, it's not you it's after!
Only I have the right to face you!
Yato! It's not charging! It's going to use its tailspin!
Out of the way!
Urghh—
Yato!
You! I told you to stay out of my way! Why did you come for me?
Forget that! Worry about the Rathalos!
Meow! It's coming fur me!
Noir Corne! Help me! Mrowwww!
I-I'm coming!
I'm here too!
Mrow! I dodged it! I'm holding on! I'm fine! I'm okay!
Take this, you monster!
Scholar, let go!
I can't! If I do, I'll get eaten!
Just listen to me! I'll catch you!
Mroaww! I couldn't catch him!
Alright! Got you, Scholar!
My blade! Argh, what's going on?! It's stuck!
Mrow! You two...
Noir Corne! We—
Aaaahhh! Why are we in the air?!
Corne!
Ah, damn it! This fire!
Are you just going to stand and watch? Think of a way to strike it down!
Aho!
Without my Flash Bombs, I cant think of anything... mrow.
No, that's impossible. I can still—
Stop chasing it, your meowjesty! You won't make it!
But—
We need to get somewhere safe right away! I still have a plan!
The campsite... It's burning...
All the equipment's gone...
If my hunch is correct, the Rathalos must have retreated to a cave somewhere in this area... Mrow.
A cave?
Right. Ever since I arrived, I've been tracking the Rathalos and observing its actions. I've seen it enter a cave with my own eyes... Mrow.
My apologies... I've been trying to rid myself of this distracting habit, but purrhaps it's in my blood... I simply can't stop meowing... mrow.
But I digress. I can take the two of you there... mrow.
It's our only option. Please do.
And Kashiwau, if you want to fight the Rathalos again...
You have no choice but to come with us.
Mrrooooooww!
Aaaaaaaaaaaahhh!
Mrrooooooww!
Mrrowaaaaah... Now you've got me mrowing!
Mrrow! We're falling!
What are you talkin—Argh, the wind's too strong! My mask!
We're falling!
I'm holding on as tight as I can! You won't fall!
Rathalos! The Rathalos is falling!
The mask is covering my eyes! I can't see anything!
Noir Corne! Noir Cornnnne! L-Look what the R-Ra-Rathalos is charging toward!
T-Toward what?!
We're about to crash!
Hold on... Finally, my mask's back in place!
Ahh! We're going to crash!
Meow! My notes... My tail... All fine. Thank heavens!
Where are we? It's dark here...
Corne...! Noir Corne! Are you still alive?
Mrrow... I can only see half your body there. Noir Corne, don't die...
I'm okay... but could you stop tugging on my leg?
I have a lamp in my equipment bag. Turn it on.
Lamp? What's that? Mew mean this thing?
Yeah, now flip the switch at the bottom.
Mrow! That's bright! But it's not hot at all... How do you do it?
Another thing. My horn... It's stuck in this rock. Could you come help me out?
Your horn's... stuck in the rock...! Meowhahaha!
Hey! Don't laugh!
I'm on meow way.
Climb up from over there. Ahh! Don't climb me! And definitely don't grab that!
Here I am... Is this where you're stuck? Wham!
Oww... My butt.
Where's the Rathalos? Did you see it?
It went inside.
The opening of this cave's too high up. It'd take us too much work to climb up without help. We need to find a way to signal Yato, but we also can't lose track of the Rathalos...
Wait, where are we anyway?
I was going to ask mew!
The Rathalos went down the cave, and the cave only further down... Maybe it's connected to the one closer to the village. Looks like we'll have to head that way to check it out.
Hey, Scholar! Wait up! What's the rush?
Meow! We need to hurry!

There are so meowny mysteries! The laws of nature here aren't all that diffurent from where we're from, but there are all these situations I can't wrap my head around! The Rathalos is acting way too oddly!
Oddly? That new Felyne mentioned something about it being abnormal, too.
I'll explain to mew as we walk!
The Rathalos burrowed itself down here... Purrhaps the cause of its odd behavior can be found here, too!
I swear this on the name of a furmer Royal Pawleontology Scriveners scholar! I will get to the bottom of this!
Noir Corne... come check this out.
I'm coming—Goodness, this stinks... Huh?
Scholar... Are these...
All animal carcasses... all shredded and torn apart by the Rathalos.
Shellbeasts, hornbeasts, fowlbeasts... so many different beasts... Did it kill all these animals for food? Are these... leftovers?
No, a Rathalos's bite can crush even bones. There is no way it would leave behind so many carcasses.
They all look very complete, too. They were killed, but there are no chew marks or signs of them having been eaten...
Come. Let's check out what's up ahead.
Alright.
Mrow! How could this be...?
What did you find?
The carcasses here have all been burnt to a crisp... They were killed and dragged all the way down here, but it still spat fire at them. There's no way it could've eaten any of these.
Is it... angry?
Look here. This, this, and this! Not one of them... It didn't eat even a single one of them!
Purrhaps... the Rathalos can't eat Terran creatures?
Could that explain uh... how it's abnormal?
I don't know... Hunger can change its behavior, but it's hard to say for sure that's the reason...
Why? I don't get it at all!
Based on my observation data, Terran creatures follow the same growth patterns as where we're from. Besides, I ate the same food as you, and there's nothing wrong with me meow!
This is just a guess, but... what if it's not caused by the food, but by the... Originium on its skin?
You mean Rathalos caught Oripathy?
—! Look at that!
What mrow?
Quick! Help me get all these animals out of the way. The dirt, too.
It stinks! Why can't you do it yourself?
Well, you tricked me into holding that fincatching rod for you. This is payback.
Mrow? *Hiss*... I'm mad! Mad, I tell you, mrow!
Wait, cut it out.
...I think I know why there are those traces of Originium on the Rathalos's body now.
Are you talking about the holes we're digging? What could they pawssibly imply?
These are tracks left behind by Originium mining. The area underneath is most likely...
An Originium mine.
If this mine is why the villagers have been going so far to hide this cave from us, then that would explain everything.
Wait! What do you mean? Meow exactly does it explain anything?

Considering Higashi's current situation and its dwindling resources... a private Originium mine that's hidden from the outside world could bring them piles of cash even if all they do is sell crude ore.
But if any outsiders—maybe even greater forces—were to find out about their hidden mine, it could very well get taken over by force. It might even put their lives in danger.
So what you're saying is, Originium is a kind of meowneral that's find in the earth, and the villagers have been digging it up?
That's right.
And you people do that on a regular basis?
Yep.
As I recall, you said Originium can cause an incurable disease called Oripathy, or even a cat-astrophic disaster that tears even the land and the sky apart...
Exactly.
So why could you pawssibly want to dig it up?
Uh... because it's an energy source, I guess?
Energy source? You can burn wood and oil for heat, and you can boil water to purr-pel machines. Can't you people do any of that fur energy?
I can't think of a good reason fur willingly exposing yourselves to something so dangerous!
What did the Doctor say again... We Terrans use Originium through Originium Arts...
Thanks to advancements in Originium engine technology, Originium became widely used as an industrial energy source. And in the past, it was also often used for casting Arts...
I don't know any Arts, though. How I can explain this to you with something else...? Oh, hand me the light.
What are mew doing with it? Mrowah! Don't take it apart! You'll purrt it out!
Here. This is what I'm talking about.
Huh? It's still lit up?
Take a look at this. This is a battery. It's what powers the light bulb up here, and that's how it's lit up.
What does that have to do with Originium?
The battery has Originium in it, too. There's also this... what do you call it... Arts Unit? That's the thing that turns the battery's Originium into electrical currents that light up the bulb.
So it lights up beclawse of Originium?
Not only that, the light bulb, the outer shell, and all the parts inside were mass produced in a factory.
Mass produced?
It's when you make the same thing over and over on a large scale. Take this exploration lamp. A huge factory can make over a thousand of them in a day.
A thousand?! That's so convenient! Could the clothes all the villagers wear pawssibly be made in those factories, too?
That's right. The factory uses machines to build these parts, and what's driving those machines is called an Originium engine.
And they need Originium to function. That's how it is in most places here.
So Terra's technology... and even its civilizations are built on a furndation of Originium.
I guess that's about it?
But our Hunters don't have lamps, or the kind of clothes mew wear. The lamp is convenient, I'll give mew that...
But even without something as dangerous as Originium, we get by just fine.
It should be pawssible to replace it with something else here too, shouldn't it?
Are these Hunters common where you guys are from?
Of course. If we leave the meownsters be, they could pose significant threats to the villagers' safety, and our livelihoods depend on the meowterials you get out of them.
So... are all the hunts these hunters go on safe?
No... Most of the time, there are dangers everywhere. You're more likely to fail a hunt than succeed.
And there's only a very small number of truly skilled hunters. When they are up against truly tricky monsters, meowst hunters end up losing their lives.
Then our Originium's actually not a whole lot different from your monsters.
Mrow? What do you mean?
Both Originium and monsters are unpreventable threats, but they both also give us the opportunity to survive.
Mrrow...
You probably won't see one, but... Catastrophes are actually very common here in Terra. Most folks live in the nomadic cities, and each city can have tens of thousands of residents.
When a Catastrophe is about to strike, the entire city starts moving.
A city with tens of thousands of residents... moving... That sounds moewvelous. How do you move something that big?
Originium. Only the energy hidden in Originium can move a nomadic city. No other energy source comes close.
I can't believe this, mrow...
We all definitely understand that using Originium can cause Catastrophes.
But... when Catastrophe strikes, if you want to survive, even if all you have nearby is a twig or branch floating in a puddle, you're bound to grab it.
It doesn't matter if it has thorns... That's the least of your worries.
Before nomadic cities were invented, before we started using Originium at the scale we do now, many more people died from Catastrophes.
Terra... sounds so scary, mrow.
Those thorns may end up cutting your fingers, but a Catastrophe's not going to end just because of your pain. You have no choice but to hold on... and hold on for dear life.
And it doesn't matter how hard you look. Until you find a smooth tree branch that won't cut you, that's all you can do.
It doesn't matter how difficult it all is. You just have to grit your teeth and live on...

Corne, do you know what the situation is like outside?
The beginnings of a Catastrophe, yeah?
Yes, there have been some obvious tells. Judging from the situation, there's still time to evacuate the villagers, but the wild beasts in the forest have already started rampaging.
We need to update each other on the situation to coordinate our actions.
Not long ago... I made the mistake of clashing with Kashiwau and letting him go off on his own.
He might be in some kind of danger right now, and I think... I should prioritize saving him over rendezvousing with you.
I'm still not clear how we'll deal with the Rathalos, but it is highly likely that he'll lose his life on his own.
It was my fault, so I absolutely cannot leave him behind.
I get you, but I gotta tell you something too.
...What is it?
Right now, we're above the Rathalos's nest, and we found out it's connected to the cave in the village...
It's an Originium mine. That's the source of the dust that the Rathalos has been spreading.
So that's what it was...
Also... we have a really good plan to deal with the Rathalos.
Oh?

If we destroy the mine and bury it in the rubble, we'll be able to take care of it once and for all. It won't be able to spread any more Oripathy, and the villagers can evacuate without any worries too.
Can you confirm the feasibility of this plan?
It was hatched by someone who's researched the mine in depth. But if we want to do this right away, just me and the Felyne Scholar won't be enough. We'll need your help too.
If we miss this opportunity, who knows what kind of accident might happen? In the worst case scenario, we'll probably be facing an unprecedented crisis, so we need you to make the call.
...Understood.
Yato...
What a dilemma we've gotten ourselves into...
Yato, listen to me.
Remember what we decided back then? We've already made our choice.
Nonsense... I never said I couldn't do it.
I'm not changing my decision. I'll go look for Kashiwau right away, while you do your best to keep the situation over there under control.
I will save his life, and I won't let the Rathalos harm anyone else either.
I'll save everyone.
Alright, be careful out there.
You too.
Die! All of you, die!
Get out of my sight!
You scamp... just why did you...?
Don't hold me back, old timer.
You truly don't have a brain up there, do you?!
A group of hunters... who know not the rules of the forest, much less respect them. And in provoking its wrath, sent all the beasts into a frenzy, trampling all over our crops.
Well, fantastic! I suppose they'll get their just deserts!
All they brought were some mining tools. There's no way they can handle that many wild beasts.
So I... I have to go in there, I can't just stand back and watch them get torn apart.
Aren't you also against the Originium mining project? This is perfect for us, is it not?
Those fools in the forest were asking for it! Just let nature consume them, as it should!
Old timer, as a hunter of the village, I of all people can't sit back at a time like this.
You idiotic, wretched, brat!
You step outside this room, and I'll break both your legs!
But you never did stop me from going.
Which is how I ended up like that.
Yes, yes, it was all me.
I caused your death... It's all my fault, I'm a terrible father.
You should feel ashamed of your incompetence.
And you must also pay for your sins.
Yes, I should, which is why I've been trying to kill all the beasts here in your stead.
Especially that most wicked, enormous, insane fire-spewing monster!
...But I am incapable of hunting it.
These hands of mine are too old to properly wield a spear, and mine eyes so clouded I can only watch milkbeasts frolic around.
Then lay down and die.
Die. Yes, that's about the only thing I am capable of now.
Kill one, and then another.
And then... I will be able to see you again.
He wanted to swing his hunting spear.
But his arms had no more strength, letting it fall to the ground.
He had no desire to retrieve it, for it had lost all purpose.
The beast bared its fangs, and was about to tear its prey apart.
Hah, denied the chance... A beast clad in scales... Now that's a sight I've not seen in...
And now, the beasts mutually rend each other apart.
Will I die beneath the claws and teeth of these monsters...?
Yato, your meowjesty, I advise mew to reconsider, for it will not be easy to get out of this.
What is that...? Someone's voice?
Just tell me how you can help me, or I'll just cut my way through.
Someone's speaking... am I just imagining things?
It's not time for you to die yet, old man.
What are you still doing here, girl?
Saving you.
You should have left this place, not come to my aid!
Fuzakeru na!
Didn't you say you were going to hunt the Rathalos? Yet you're so willing to die to some nameless beast?

Open your eyes already! The frenzied beasts are going to rush down the mountain sooner or later, and the first thing they'll trample over will be the village... Your neighbors will be forced to scatter and flee, and innocent children will die.
Are you going to just stand by and watch all of that happen?
Yoshitaka Kashiwau, you are a hunter of Roka Village. And as its only hunter, you of all people can't sit back at a time like this.
The last thing you should be doing is feeling sorry for yourself here, much less giving up your life so easily.
Wield that spear in your hands, abandon those useless obsessions, and think carefully on what a hunter's duty is!
To defend their home from the sharp claws of beasts, to desperately keep the flame of survival lit!
True, somebody will always be forced to bear the price... Hunters, as well as us... But we have both chosen this path.
Now get up!
Akira...
What was it that you said back then, to get me to let you go...
I said... that I would defeat them all.
Did you succeed?
I did, father.
Akira...
You've got a damn good spear, boy. I should hold onto it tight.
Go, and never appear before me again.
I will defeat them all.
That's enough... noise from you.
You don't speak much, girl. But when you do, you're fiercer than a mangler.
If you have the strength to talk, then stop wasting time and cover the rear.
I have no reason to take orders from a whippersnapper... Mind your own business.
Your meowjesty's words remind me so much of my time in Kokoto Village.
Before the age of the Hunters, it was the headman who first stepped up to defend the village from meownsters, earning the title of 'hero' for his bravery...
Mrow! Please do not pick me up by the scruff of the neck.
Palico, watch our right.
Do you remember the moves I spoke of earlier, your meowjesty?
Well, I've gone over them in my head a few times.
Mew must remember, the trick to using the Dual Blades to their fullest potential is to abandon all defense and enter a state alike to a ferocious beast.
Or as we call it, 'Demon Mode.'
'Demon Mode,' huh...
We move.

I never thought the cave would be so close to a volcano.
My tail is feeling so warm—
Meowch! It's hot!
It's on fire!
Now I get why you want to close the mine. We'd have done the same, in your shoes.
This place has definitely been overmined. It even has an Originium processing plant, but none of the specialized equipment you'd usually see...
This has gone way further than a tiny village can handle.
Mining so carelessly without strict safeguards in place will only result in the leakage of active Originium particles, and inevitably cause Catastrophes.
But what I don't get is...
Based on what you said, they started mining seven years ago, and the person who lead the project was your uncle, the current village headman.
So... why do the tunnels stretch so deep after just seven years? They can't possibly have dug all this themselves.
You're half-correct.
Huh?
The mining tunnels weren't dug by the villagers, they were already here before.
Remember what I said earlier, about the beast outbreak seven years ago?
Yeah, you said it was a real serious one, and that old Kashiwau's son, Akira, was also a hunter... and lost his life in it.
That was a direct consequence of the mining.
Meow!
You good, Scholar?

I'm purrfectly fine, what exactly did I trip on?
Meow!
Bones?!
Yeah, that's a whole lotta bones, plus teeth, and... claws?
They have been dead fur a long time...
Wait, this form... It must have been a large carnivorous creature! This is my furst time seeing one here!
Judging from its remains, it would have been covered in scales and have well-developed forelimbs with long and sharp claws. So it most pawbably was good at digging holes!
An arma-clawbeast.
That's their name. A type of predator that once inhabited this region. They were social creatures that would dig their nests in the mountains.
This mine was actually one of their nests, and they built majestic palaces over the years while tunneling through the surrounding Originium veins.
But we haven't seen a single one down here, or in the forest.
That's because... they disappeared seven years ago.
Disappeared?
Disappeared? Fur real?
The very last trace of their species in this area is the pile of skeletons before you.
How... How exactly did something like that happen?
Back when this Originium mine was newly discovered, Akira Kashiwau was firmly against the project.
He reckoned destroying the arma-clawbeasts' nests would net unpredictable consequences, and that Originium mining itself wasn't exactly safe either.
On the other hand, my uncle and the other villagers believed that they desperately needed the potential profits to change their grueling way of life.
So concealing it from Akira, they and the other hunters banded together to exterminate all the arma-clawbeasts in the region. In order to freely mine the Originium.
But the slaughter resulted in the surviving arma-clawbeasts rampaging through the forest, leading to the beast outbreak that year.
So many innocent lives were lost... just for the sake of opening a mine.
You must have seen my uncle's attitude, yes?
To him, the Rathalos is simply the manifestation of vengeance from all the beasts he's slaughtered. He definitely has dreams about Akira's death on the regular too.
His closest friend, his apprentice, carried out the will of a hunter to the very end... and died for his sake.
And now that Akira's predictions have come true... naturally he's terrified.
Akira died for the headman's sake? I thought he lost his life protecting the village...?
The outbreak wasn't threatening the village, but was closer to the mine.
He was beset by frenzied beasts whose numbers far surpassed any regular outbreak we'd seen.
Oh, we're here.
Originium rocks were clustering around the lava bubbling in the cave.
The King of the Skies lifted its head.
The insignificant Oni looked down.
Their eyes each reflected the other's gaze.
Chikushou-me.
It's surrounded by a bunch of Originium rocks.
Since you didn't want to deal with it right now, take care not to get too close.
If we accidentally anger it, we'll be in deep trouble.
Got it. Scholar... where you at?
The Rathalos... seems to be using the Originium fur its lair.
This is impawssible to comprehend...
It looks like... it's in a lot of pain. Is it because of the Originium on it?
Most pawbably, and there seems to be substantially more particles compurred to our previous encounter.
Right now it's more or less an oversized source of pollution spreading Originium dust wherever it goes.
My hypawthesis is that... the Rathalos most pawbably was just trying to survive, and ended up nesting here.
But being deep in the mines, it's constantly exposed to Originium.
When it returns to the forest to feed, the flames it spews while hunting will in turn trigger the clusters on its body, dispersing purrticles everywhere.
So it's a victim of Originium too.
Must you hunt it, Noir Corne?
The Originium is too much of a danger to leave alone, and considering the safety of both the village and ourselves, hunting it is the best way of handling the situation.
But if we can deal with just the clusters... I just need a little more time! I'll bring out my binoculars...
What else could there be...
Mrow? Those tracks are...
Scholar, come quick! You're too far out, the ground's too unstable over there!
Mrow?
Meow!
Haha... caught ya.
Mrow.. I was so afuraid!
Noir Corne! Why didn't mew warn me earlier?
Did mew see that?
Uh-huh.
The bignawculars just bounced off the Rathalos's head.
Ah.
Sparks are coming out of its jaws.
Just run already! The mine is gonna be destroyed!
Run fur it!
I'm running!
If it triggers all the Originium here, the anomalies are definitely going to spike, and then...
It'll be a Catastrophe!

lines.st: A black mist shrouds the sky, and the mountains and rivers burst.
Wind scales the peaks, and flames rise like a crimson tide.
Vegetation burns to ashes, and life into coal.
The village gates swing open, and the houses collapse.
All life cowers, and the heavens fall.

lines.x: Nghh... hah... hah...
They're dodging my slashes so easily.
How foolish. You clearly lack a hunter's intuition. Their weak point is the soft patch of skin in their jaws.
Stab straight in, so you can slit the throat.
...Got it.
(Sixfold Slash!)
A hit! Ah...
Have a taste of this, kono yarou!
Aghh—
We did it!
Be careful of the rear, mew two!
Nanja korya?!
(Twofold Slash!)
Hmph...
You're welcome.
Are my hands... losing their strength?
On my way to a certain village, I heard tales of an endless stream of dragons, but to... purrsonally witness a similar event.
The beast outbreak is showing no signs of abating. If we remain trapped here, we'll eventually collapse from exhaustion. We have to find a way out.
If we can make our way to those tall trees over there, we can make use of the canopy's height to avoid the rampage.
I have an idea.
What's this?
This is the powder I used to trigger the hornbeasts earlier, in hopes of luring out the Rathalos. But I used too much and lost control of the herd.
Using it on people is unheard of, and probably suicidal. But right now.... this might be our only method of drawing them away.
But that means...
Yes, whoever is affected by it will be beset by the entire horde... But as long as we can make our way through, it will be worth it... Probably...
No... Artisan, do you still have that rope from earlier?
Yes! I made so meowch of it!
Good... it's long and tough enough to support the weight of multiple people. If we tie it to the tree, we can use it as a makeshift grappling hook to retrieve whoever's acting as bait.
Which will be me, so if you would...
No, I must be the bait.
I won't allow it. It's too dangerous to let you get surrounded by the horde again. If you sacrifice yourself here, wouldn't that make my efforts to save you meaningless?
I don't know if I'd be able to rescue you with these old hands of mine, but I can at least make sure not to croak before you rescue me.
I have faith in you, girl.
...Fine, let's do this.
Come, you dastards! Over here!
Yes, just like that! Chase me like the lunatics you are!
Now's my chance!
(Flurry Rush!)
Hrrh—haah!
It worked... purrfectly!
Deploy the grappling hook immediately, I'll go retrieve Kashiwau!
These beasts just charge straight at me with wild abandon.
We really lured them away...I can't believe it.
There's simply so many of them...
That day... that day seven years ago, was also like this...
Brat... Is this how you felt, that night? Did you... die to something like this?
Was this... what you saw in your final moments?
Surrounded by these beasts, encircled by their jaws, drowning in their saliva.
You must have been slaying them one after another with this spear, just like this.
But no matter how many you killed, there were always more of these damnable beasts, wave after relentless wave.
Ngh—Agh! Begone!
Kuso! They saw you as a mere slab of meat to be divided between themselves, no longer among the living.
And knowing you, brat, you probably just kept your mouth shut, rather than calling for help.
Simply brandishing this lance till your strength failed you, till you could wield it no longer.
Collapsing on some rocks, slowly falling to your knees... Yet the beasts never ceased their advance!
Ah... so that's how it was.
Kashiwau, grab my hand!
What are you blanking out for?! Quickly!
Got you!
Palico, pull the rope!
Finally...
Not yet, your meowjesty... The branches over there have broken...
Meowny more beasts rush over as we speak!
Chikushou, is there anything else we can do?
Your meowjesty, look! The beasts are scattering all of a sudden!
Mrow... A noise from the sky.
The Rathalos soars through the sky! And that's...
Nantekotta...
A Catastrophe...
The gale carelessly bound both land and sky together with flame, like an ignorant life devouring everything in its path.
Trees were but weeds within the tornado of fire, and mountains crumbled to rubble.
The most fearless of warriors were powerless to stand against it, and the most devout prayers echoed to no avail.
It had arrived, the land's retribution.
Jump down! Brace for impact!
Is everyone alright?
I'm fine.
I'm... purrfectly fine as well.
The sky is alight... Pillars of crimson flame... Kuso, what a truly terrifying sight.
...I've read about a similar case on the landship before.
A hurricane unleashed by a Catastrophe encircled a mountain on fire, becoming a ferocious firestorm.
As it moves, the vortex pulls from its surroundings. And with everything combustible in this forest... I can't imagine the consequences.
Why... Why did the Catastrophe strike so soon?
The center of the firestorm... it's near the mine.
The mine?!
Taste my blade!
Hey! So this is where you guys were. See, Scholar? Just like I said...
That's enough yapping, Noir Corne. I expect a full report soon.
Aight.
...Old Kashiwau? What are you doing here?
I could ask you the same thing, Mirai.
You can hardly call this fortunate, but at least we managed to escape the horde thanks to the Catastrophe.
I don't know what the situation in the village is right now, but the core of the Catastrophe is still quite a ways away and moving fairly slowly. However, that's not the case with the beast outbreak.
Any ideas on how to return to the village as soon as possible?
Ah, if that's still nearby... Maybe we can use it to descend the mountain quickly!
It has not been used for a long time. I can't be sure if it still works.
So, uh, planning on letting the rest of us in on this?
There's a railcar. We used it a lot when the mines were just opening, and it made things real convenient, but after the cave was repaired we more or less abandoned it.
Don't worry, it should still work fine. It was the very first thing I designed, after all.
Weren't you an ecologist? I'm not sure I should trust your skills as a railcar engineer...
Kashiwau, our next battle won't be any easier, so I hope you're prepared.
I don't suppose you'd let this old man loaf about for once?
Please, by all means. I fully intend to respect your opinion.
Oh?
I'm aware that I tend to ignore the ideas of those around me and insist on doing things my way. And that this is a behavior I should correct.
The mistakes I've made were precisely because of that, and I should also apologize for what I said earlier.
I'm sorry for my unproductive words, without knowing anything about your background. I did not intend to hurt you.
Hm...
So will you accept my apology?
Fine... if it pleases you.
Good, then that's settled.
Girl...
Earlier you said you understood me... what did you mean by that?
Ah, that... It's a bit of a long story.
If it's a bother, just pretend I didn't ask.
No, I don't mind. You see, before joining Rhodes Island, I was an assassin.
Nani?
A literal killer, acting on orders to take the lives of my people, day and night.
Until one day, I looked at my bloodstained hands and felt nothing but fear in my heart. The next day, I was tasked to dispose of a mother and daughter, but chose to protect them instead.
Because I didn't want to be a killer anymore. That was also the day I met Noir Corne, who listened to my story and chose the same path.
But I'd made a mistake. It wasn't just a matter of refusing to kill.

The pair I saved were so frightened of me that I could only leave them in a safe place. And while in the moment I felt only the weightless relief of not taking a life, I had forgotten something important...
That the only end awaiting them was to be killed by someone else.
Do you... regret it?
Yes. For a long time after that, I... often dreamt of them. They would ask me why I had left them to die.
I didn't want to hurt innocents anymore, but I still ended up indirectly cutting their lives short.
...I used to wonder if I was even capable of protecting anyone at all.
Luckily, I had help... Thanks to him, I made my decision.
You mean the boy over there?
Yes.
Heh.
He scolded me—a rare occurrence—and said...
'The past is the past... All your remorse, all the sins you carry, make up for them with your future.'
I took him for just an oddball, but I suppose he's got a proper head on after all.
What he said seemed right to me, and since then I haven't given it much thought.
We decided to make it our mission to protect others, and he dragged me along to join Rhodes Island. And because of our similar objectives, we're still working together even now.
This must be some company, to hiring on people like you.
So protecting others is your way of atoning for your past?
You might say it started like that, but I've had a few additional insights along the way.
I've seen too much life and death. There are many reasons people might surrender their lives, and some even seek death out of ignorance.
You could say I stubbornly impose my will on others, but only because of my duty to protect your lives.
Life in this land is not meant to end so easily, but to be lived and experience all its possibilities.
So I will continue my efforts.
I don't want to regret anything, or to see people forced to gaze only at ruins.
So I refuse to leave you alone.
Yato! Kashiwau! We found the railcar and it's still working!
Hey, what're you both looking at me like that for? Is there something on my mask?
It's nothing. We'll be right over.
Anyway, I look forward to cooperating with you in the upcoming battle, Kashiwau.
(Holds out hand)
I've told you this so many times already, that's my quarry.
You need only watch from the sidelines and applaud my brilliance.
I'll just pretend I didn't hear that.
The path you've chosen is not an easy one.
All I can do is wish you the best.
Likewise.
Hurry it up, everyone!
But...
You should run too, Ritou! Money isn't as important as your life.
Shut up!
I'll delay the old man!
What are you standing around for?
Can I take it you've given up on treating your sister?
But... Alright.
Kusso...
*Sobbing*...
Mom? Where are you?
Where are you...
Mom... don't leave me here...
(Flurry Rush!)
In the nick of time!
Is the child okay?
Let me see. All four limbs attached, no external wounds... does it hurt anywhere?
Ouch... your armor's spiky...
Oops, sorry.
My child!
Mom!
Thank you... Thank you so much for saving my child!
Stay away from the forest. There are wild beasts in the area, and they're increasing in numbers. It's not safe here.
Yato... I don't think they came out here because they wanted to.
No! There's netting between the village and the forest. I reinforced it myself not long ago. How could there be beasts here?
I need to go take a look.
Calm down. Has the evacuation started?
No... There's no evacuation. The mine exploded, the sky started burning... there's nothing left.
Everyone's running. We all panicked when we heard that beasts were coming, but we don't know where to go.
Why is it so chaotic? What happened?
I tried to pull Naoki away from the crowd, but then a bunch of them ran straight at us. Naoki was gone by the time I caught my breath.
Someone intentionally damaged the netting, letting in the beasts.
Ano yarou... Where is Takii?
The headman is—
Here they come again, Corne!
I'll hold them off with my shield... Argh, whatever, a sword's fine!
Kashiwau, please take these two to a safe place and see if you can help out in the village. Corne and I will stop the beasts.
I don't need you to tell me that. Let's go Mirai... Mirai?
I think she already went in.
How could it have come so quickly? Wasn't it supposed to take more time for the Catastrophe to form?
Noshige, Inoue, get everybody together and take them to the shelter I told you about! It's safer there. We'll evacuate as a group once we have everybody!
Good thing we'd prepared for this day... What you said came true again.
It's burning...
The mountains are covered in smoke... the sky's on fire... the mine's gone...
What are you doing? Grab your things and get out of here!
My livelihood, my life, it's all gone...
Headman... will we have to go back to our old life, now that the mine's all burned up?
Now's not the time for that!
Gone... everything's gone...
Why are you panicking like that? The Catastrophe isn't even here yet.
Beasts! The beasts are coming!
Beasts! And so close! What happened to the protective netting?
Ritou, get over here! What's going on over there?
Headman! The netting on the west side is broken! The beasts are in the village! What do we do?
What in blazes is going on here?
Everybody, calm down! Take the bare minimum of what you need, gather at the shelter in the northeast, and wait for evacuation! The beasts can't get in there.
Headman... why is there a shelter in the village?
What?
Did you already know this was going to happen?
This... happened because you closed the mine, didn't it?
H-Headman?
Headman!
What you on about, Ritou? You know that isn't true!
This is no time to be fooling around! Lives are at stake here!
Don't just stand there, folks! Head to the shelter!
No, this is important! Everything we've worked for is gone! We need justice!
Why did the mine have to be closed? Why did this disaster happen right afterward?
Y-Yeah! You closed it for 5 days out of the blue for a 'maintenance check,' and now the mine's gone, and the whole mountain is burning!
Did you close the mine and keep the truth hidden from the others because of that monster that showed up down there? Is that the cause of this disaster?
We could have worked together to deal with it!
It was your idea to keep it a secret, to prevent a panic.
And don't think I don't know about your little side business. I know how much you've pocketed ever since your family started handling the transactions.
If you have the slightest bit of conscience left, stop delaying the evacuation!
Then how do you explain the shelter? You must have planned this in advance... You're the one who wants to hoard the wealth of the mine all to yourself!
You even blew up the cave... You killed those two doctors who came to investigate the Oripathy!
Headman...
What did you do, Headman?
Not you too... Ritou...
Yes, I'll admit I've wanted to close the mine for a long time. I knew that overexploitation of the mine was bound to bring disaster. The shelter was built in preparation for this day.
Why? Because we're over-reliant on Originium mining. Originium particles have already entered the environment. The danger has been slowly building for a while now!
It was only a matter of time before Catastrophe struck and we'd have to abandon the mine, but I couldn't get everyone to give up on it before. We all benefitted too much from the Originium trade.
That day simply came a little sooner than expected, that's all.
And yes, I closed the mine because of that unknown creature.
You all know that I used to be a hunter. I judged that it wasn't something we could easily handle, and we couldn't afford to fight it in the tunnels.
Ishidori and the others have already been infected with Oripathy. People would have died if we'd continued to dig. The responsibility for all of your lives falls on my shoulders.
...Which is the same reason I'm telling you to evacuate now.
Mine or not, the most important thing is that we're alive.
But then things would go back to how they used to be...
Cold nights... howling in the forest... blood, cold, hunger... fear... no! I don't want to go back to that!
So what if we're alive?! Where's the hope? I'd rather die than go back to living like that!
What are you saying... get ahold of yourself!
He's right! We won't go back!
It was you who got us started on mining Originium in the first place! It's all your fault!
You ruined everything!
You've ruined the village! Ruined all our lives!
This man must be made to pay! We all agree, don't we?
Enough of this!
There's a Catastrophe right on your doorstep!
Haven't we already paid enough of a price? Are we going to lose even more lives just for this meaningless venting?
Mirai! Why are you back?
Oh look, another troublemaker. The apple doesn't fall far from the tree.
The frightened beasts are heading down the mountain, the netting's been sabotaged, and someone's trying to stir up chaos...
All to force us to wait for death in despair, and abandon the hope we could have had.
Oh...
And we still can have, away from the Originium mines, without having to rely on hunting either.
That's why I came back from the city.
Liar! You were the one who wanted to close the mine and ruin our lives!
Yes, because Originium is dangerous and hard to control. I even considered blowing up the mine.
But I also understand that we owe our livelihood to it.
Do you remember back when we were trying to climb out of poverty? Were we in despair then?
Was it really the Originium that got us to where we are today?
We seized our chance to escape poverty because we had the determination to look for a way, and the courage to expose ourselves to Originium.
Y... Yeah.
Since ancient times, hunters have made a living by fighting beasts, back when there was no Originium. Many of them died, but we survived as a people.
Courage and hope come hand-in-hand. And we've never abandoned our courage...
So hope will always appear by our side.
Don't listen to her! She was the one who wanted to close the mine! And now she's destroyed the mine, she practically admitted it!
But Mirai only tried to convince us to close it because overexploitation would cause a Catastrophe. And now that really happened...
We were wrong to doubt her...
You're familiar with the plant in this flask, aren't you? Among the goods that we trade with the outside, the Suzuka herb is second only to Originium in terms of trade volume.
It only grows in certain areas, and in small numbers. We've had to risk life and limb to harvest it.
But I came back to study the possibility of cultivating it, and planting it outside its native habitat. This one I'm holding right here is my greatest breakthrough.
It can survive outside of these mountains. It's the first brick that will lay the foundation of our future as a village.
But first, we need to survive.
Survive...
Yeah, what were we thinking? We fought so hard to get to this point. We can't just die here.
No! We'll lose all our income without the mine—
Aah!
Who... gah...
Open your mouth again, and I'm sticking your head in the mud.
This entire conversation is a waste of time.
This man damaged the netting, tried to lure in beasts to cause chaos, then distracted everyone from what was going on.
While on the other side of the village, he had some people moving his assets out, something he clearly planned ahead of time. I've already taken care of them.
You will now head to the shelter in an orderly line and await evacuation. Reinforcements from Rhodes Island will be arriving soon.
Now, you can walk there yourselves, or I can knock you out and have someone else carry you. Choose.
Er... thank you.
There's a beast outbreak, and they're approaching the village. That's the biggest threat we're facing right now.
We'll handle the beasts. I can't guarantee we'll get all of them, but we'll do what we can to ensure your safety.
No, please stay here and protect the evacuating villagers. You're the only ones who can.
And take care of Mirai for me.
Headman! Where are you going?
I'm the headman of Roka Village, and the leader of its hunters.
The beasts have emerged from their forests, so I'll fight them to my last breath, even if I'm on my own!
Honey, take Tsuyumaru to the shelter.
I think I left my machete in the backyard?
Yes, it's there... come back safely!
The headman's always treated our family well. It's high time we repaid him!
Yes, we're with him, whether it's in the mines or in the forests. We've always been hunters. Take up your spears!
We'll protect our own village and our own families!
Headman! Wait for us!
I'm going too!
Mom, didn't dad said there were no hunters anymore?
No, Sumiko. The hunters have always been here, ready to step forward whenever danger approaches.
Hmph... and now they're putting on a show. They're no hunters.
I'm the only one...
Hyah! Gah!
(Panting)
Get down, old man!
Die!
What?
Not you! The beast!
Well, get down! I'm setting off my Originium Arts!
Grab my hand. Are you okay?
I'm fine.
What was that? Those beasts went down in the blink of an eye...
Originium Arts using this Arts Unit. My own special trick.
Tch... parlor tricks.
The traps will slow the rest. Leave them to Sumoto's group. We can head over to the other side, where the defenses are thinner... Take it easy, old man.
Cut the crap.
What's with that look on your face?
No, just thinking back to the days when us hunters fought side by side.
It's been seven years, and this is the first time you haven't told me to get lost or called me a traitor.
I... I didn't think you would really take up...
Akira's hunting spear. You can say it. I know you were Akira's mentor. You didn't think I would go kill those beasts?
You weren't a hunter at the time, and you objected to Akira becoming one. His sacrifice changed you...
I'm glad you noticed.
Old man, there's something... Perhaps you've misunderstood all this time, and I wasn't sure how to tell you.
I didn't abandon him to die.
Lure powder.
You knew?
I'm his father.
That idiot sacrificed himself to protect your mine.
I still remember the look on his face that day, his eyes, his every move...
The cries of the beasts were everywhere. He opened his mouth to say something, but it was drowned out by the noise. I remember his pale lips...
Oh...
Could he have been saying...
Akira!
Kusso, where did all these beasts come from? What did you do?
Don't tell me you—
Stay away, master! Don't follow me, no matter what!
Come back! We'll stop them here!
No, master! You should know better than anyone!
We can't stop an outbreak like this... many people will be hurt, even killed.
The Originium mine would be destroyed. Everything you've worked for would be lost. I can't let that happen.
Weren't you against the mine? Just let it burn!
Come back! Your life matters more!
The beasts are gathering.
Time is short, master.
Yes, I was against the mine. Originium is unknown and dangerous. It will bring disaster we can't even predict.
I also can't forgive the taking of innocent lives. This was the inevitable result of you failing to respect nature and letting greed take over.
But I also remember the day we went into the city together and saw the high-rise buildings. The bright lights and shining signs, all made possible by Originium...
Originium is valuable. It will lift the village out of poverty, become the pillar of our livelihood... We've come this far. Don't let this opportunity go to waste.
Akira!
Wasn't it you who taught me that a hunter must fight for the survival of his clan?
Out of the way, you damned beasts!
This beast outbreak is the wrath of nature.
But I'm also fighting for survival. We stare each other in the eyes as equals.
Promise me one last thing, master.
Oh...
Lead the others.
Survive.
Come back, Akira!
And please pass this on to my father, that stubborn old timer.
He said...
'I'm sorry, father.'
Hmph... I've had enough of your tall tale. He never called me father.
That brat...
Argh!
(Deep breath)
But I...
Only the old man's back is visible.
But he could hear the sound of water dripping.
Tears that had been forced back for too long, finally overflowing.
I miss him.
Up above!
That monster... it's coming.
The beasts are coming again! Chikushou, how could there be so many!
We don't have enough hands!
You stay here! Set up those traps and stop the beasts!
THAT one is mine.
I'm a hunter. That's my quarry.
Yato! Here comes the Rathalos!
I knew it.
After our previous encounters, it now sees all humans as a threat.
It landed near the Kashiwau house, and it's getting closer!
The reinforcements are still pretty far off. Not all the villagers have made it to the shelter either.
This is the worst possible timing... You oversee the evacuation. I'll—
Over there, Yato! Beasts! I see five of them!
The stampede is coming. The hunters' defenses can't stop all of them. We must protect the evacuating villagers.
What do we do then? Just sit here and wait for the Rathalos? That will only make things worse!
I'm thinking... We need a way to stop the Rathalos for a while, at least until all the villagers are safe...
Kashiwau...
Kashiwau? But we don't even know where he is. And he's just one man.
I see him, near the hut.
He's close to the Rathalos! Yato, maybe we should—
We'll have time to complete the evacuation if he can delay it.
You mean... we're not helping him?
We just have to trust him.
(Opens a can of oil)
You think so too, eh? Today's a good day. The heavens burn red.
So many things have happened lately. A little girl came back all grown up, stirring up all kinds of trouble.
A firebreathing monster appeared out of nowhere, and two outsiders went in trouble near the forest.
Then beasts came rushing up, their mine blew up, a Catastrophe struck, and they couldn't even run away properly.
And the funniest part? People keep coming to dig up my past from the mud and rub my face in it.
They all say it's for my sake, but each shard of it they dig up cuts me open, piece by piece.
Noir Corne had the right idea. The truth isn't important. Let the past stay in the past.
Let the dead stay dead. Burn it all, leave nothing behind.
He hears the sobbing of flames, swallowing up the fragments of the past.
The ashes of time drift before his eyes, burning away the gaze of regret.
Burn.
This fire is so beautiful.
You'd have done the same, wouldn't you, Akira?
I'll take the next step.
Hey! Over here!
Even the corners of your jaws are singed. Your scales are full of scars. You big ugly...
What's that? Sparks from your mouth? Are you angry?
Don't look away. Your enemy's right here.
Look at me. Yes. That's right.
Be angry. Be angrier.
Come on!
Face me, monster!

eps.name: Battle! Blazin' Soul of a Warrior!

lines.x: He kneeled on the ground, right hand still clutching the spear planted in the dirt.
His body was gravely injured, but he felt no pain, perhaps because it was pulsing from all directions and his aging nerves were too dulled feel it.

Or perhaps his skin was too scorched, to the point it could not comprehend the pain, the searing temperatures evaporating any kind of liquid or vapor, his blood instantly hardening to black scabs on his body.
His throat felt like it was on fire, with a strangely sweet scent emanating from it, and he suddenly felt a convulsion from his abdomen as something surged up.
Hggh—Aghk—
Blech—bah! Kuso, this is so disgusting.
A huge roar rumbled in his eardrums and his consciousness managed to peel away from the muddy chaos.
He raised his head, staring at the enormous behemoth rearing up before him.
He stared into its eyes.
Hoh...it's you.
Yes... I remember now....
Images from mere minutes ago flashed through his mind, and he seized the fleeting opportunity in-between the flames to hurl the spear towards the Rathalos's head.
He hit his target, but at the cost of failing to dodge the beast's retaliatory charge.
Hahah... hahahaha!
Blood! Haha, do you feel it? The pain?
That was me! I made you bleed! How does it feel to be wounded?
I've known all along... those scales on your skull aren't so tough after all. I can spot your vulnerability at a glance!
You are not invincible... You can bleed, and you will fall!
Wait... Hey!
You! Where are you going?!
I just wounded you! You can't run away now!
I can still fight! We haven't battled it out yet!
He leaned on his hunting spear, trying to prop up his body, but his knee would only stay at an angle.
The spear's shaft was sunk deep in the ground, and his shadow trembled violently.
You can't leave here! I won't... let you go...
I managed to make you bleed this time, so next...
I will plunge my spear into your heart!
He raised the spear up high, and perhaps because he thought it was his final chance, his crooked body exploded with unimaginable strength.
He burst into a run, and once again charged at the life he could only look up to.
Aaaaaaaaahh—
*cough*...
I'm... not dead yet...
Chikushou... one more time!
His right hand was still holding the spear in a death grip, nails digging into his palm.
He hit his thighs in desperation, but the muscles merely trembled unresponsively.
This time, he had truly exhausted any last trace of strength in his body.
The spear slipped from his hand.
Get up! Stand up!
...Damn it!
Get! Up!
His eyes widened.
He saw it.
A young child raising his bow and arrow, facing the Rathalos.
His thin arms trembled, but his gaze never wavered.
M-Monster...don't get any closer to Mr. Kashiwau!
I am Kazuya! I'm also a hunter of this village!
I won't let you destroy it! We will stop you here!
Corne!
I'm here!
I got him! The kid should be fine!
Scholar, go take the kid and Kashiwau somewhere safe!
Mew got it!
Meow got the cart here!
The Rathalos... is injured? By this hunter and a Terran spear?
This hunter... his body is so light, where did he get all that strength from?
Mister...
You're really a brave one, and I'd even call you a proper hunter, but how about we let the adults handle it today?
The flames blazed brilliantly.
At that very moment, another bruised body stood before the Rathalos.
She bent down and stretched out an arm, picking up the spear from the ground.
And then drove it firmly into the ground.
She straightened her back.
Thank you for your time, Kashiwau.
Now please, take a good rest on the sidelines.
As for what comes next...
Leave it to us.
I'm ready!
Battle! Commeownce!
